results.name: Lunge Front Kick
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Lift your right leg to perform a front kick, extending your leg straight out in front of you.
As you bring your right leg back down, step it behind you into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your left heel to stand back up, returning to the starting position. Repeat the movement on the same side or alternate legs for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle during the lunge to avoid strain.
Perform the front kick with control, avoiding any jerky movements to prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you perform the front kick and inhaling as you lower into the lunge.
results.description: Lunge Front Kick is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Lunge Pulses Bodyweight
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart. Step your right foot forward into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
From the lunge position, perform small pulses by slightly raising and lowering your hips in a controlled manner.
Continue pulsing for the desired number of repetitions or duration, keeping your core engaged and maintaining balance.
Return to the starting position by pushing through your right heel and repeat the exercise on the opposite leg.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle and does not extend past your toes to avoid strain.
Use a controlled motion and avoid bouncing to maintain muscle tension and effectiveness.
Perform the pulses with control, avoiding any jerky movements to prevent injury.
results.description: Lunge Pulses Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

results.name: Lunge Reverse With Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing the middle of the resistance band under your left foot. Hold the handles of the resistance band at shoulder height with your elbows bent and facing the floor.
Step your right leg back into a reverse lunge, bending both knees to lower your right knee towards the floor while keeping your left knee aligned with your ankle.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, bringing your right leg forward.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides to work the other leg.
tips: Exhale as you push back up to the starting position and inhale as you lower into the lunge.
Focus on engaging your glutes and quadriceps throughout the movement.
Ensure your front knee does not extend past your toes to avoid joint strain.
results.description: Lunge Reverse With Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Shoulders.

results.name: Lunge Rotation Left and Right Bodyweight
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms bent at your sides, hands close to your torso.
Step your right foot forward into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
Rotate your torso to the right, bringing your arms to the right side, then rotate your torso to the left, bringing your arms to the left side.
Return your torso to the center and push through your right heel to return to the starting position. Repeat the movement on the opposite leg. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle and does not extend past your toes to avoid strain.
Keep your back straight and your chest lifted to maintain proper posture.
Perform the rotations with control, avoiding any jerky movements to prevent injury.
results.description: Lunge Rotation Left and Right Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Lunge to Knee Drive Left Bodyweight
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Step your left foot back into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your right heel to stand back up, simultaneously driving your left knee up towards your chest.
Return your left leg to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Switch sides and repeat the movement with your right leg stepping back.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle and does not extend past your toes to avoid strain.
Perform the knee drive with control, avoiding any jerky movements to prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you drive your knee up and inhaling as you lower into the lunge.
results.description: Lunge to Knee Drive Left Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Step your right foot back into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your left heel to stand back up, simultaneously driving your right knee up towards your chest.
Return your right leg to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Switch sides and repeat the movement with your left leg stepping back.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle and does not extend past your toes to avoid strain.
Perform the knee drive with control, avoiding any jerky movements to prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you drive your knee up and inhaling as you lower into the lunge.
results.description: Lunge to Knee Drive Right Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

results.name: Lunges Alternate Leg With Pause Bodyweight
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.

Step your right foot forward into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor. Pause for a moment in this position.

Push through your right heel to return to the starting position, then step your left foot forward into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee nearly touches the floor. Pause for a moment in this position.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position. Alternate legs for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle and does not extend past your toes to avoid strain.
Perform each lunge with control, pausing briefly to enhance muscle engagement.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you push back to the starting position and inhaling as you step forward into the lunge.
results.description: Lunges Alternate Leg With Pause Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Bodyweight Same Leg Lunge (Side View)
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.

Step your right foot forward into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor. Pause for a moment in this position.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat the lunge with your right leg for the desired number of repetitions before switching to your left leg.
tips: Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you push back to the starting position and inhaling as you step forward into the lunge.
Keep your back straight and your chest lifted to maintain proper posture.
Use a controlled motion when bringing your leg back to the starting position to maintain balance.
results.description: Bodyweight Same Leg Lunge (Side View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Lying Leg Curl Machine
instructions: Lie face down on the lying leg curl machine, positioning your legs under the padded lever, just above your ankles. Adjust the machine so that your knees are just off the edge of the bench.
Grasp the handles on the sides of the machine for stability and keep your back flat against the bench.
Curl your legs up towards your glutes by bending your knees, squeezing your hamstrings at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the padded lever back to the starting position with control, fully extending your legs. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips pressed against the bench throughout the exercise to isolate the hamstring muscles.
Avoid using momentum; let your muscles do the work.
Exhale as you curl your legs up and inhale as you lower them back down.
results.description: Lying Leg Curl Machine is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

results.name: Med Ball Front Squat Raise
instructions: Stand holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
As you stand, raise the ball straight out in front of you to shoulder height.
Bring it back to your chest and repeat.
tips: Keep your arms straight on the raise.
Keep your heels on the floor.
results.description: Med Ball Front Squat Raise is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Core.
